title: Formal Methods Transfer: Applying Model Checking to Verify AI Attack Plan Correctness Before Execution

original_idea.body:
# Formal Methods Transfer: Applying Model Checking to Verify AI Attack Plan Correctness Before Execution

**Problem:** AI agents generate attack plans that are often syntactically correct but semantically invalid (e.g., planning to exploit a vulnerability that doesn't exist on the target). There is no methodology for formally verifying attack plan feasibility before costly execution attempts.

**Direction:** Adapt lightweight model checking or specification language techniques (e.g., Alloy, TLA+ simplified) to specify a network state model. Before executing each step, use a programmatic constraint checker to verify the planned action is feasible given the current known state. Measure whether pre-execution verification reduces wasted tool invocations and increases net step completion rate.

**Why it matters:** Attack plan verification could dramatically improve AI offensive efficiency (fewer wasted attempts) — but also has a dual-use defensive application: using the same formal methods to verify that a planned attack cannot succeed before it is launched, enabling proactive defensive hardening.

**Relevant context:** Context relay paper (NDSS 2026) addresses long-running agent context management. AWS multi-agent architecture (2025) used specialized planning sub-agents. Formal methods in cybersecurity is well-established but not applied to AI agent planning verification. Menlo Ventures (2025) identified planning as a key bottleneck in agentic security tools.
